subject: SLA exception request — customer-operated edge controls (SkyRover)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@skyrover.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: carve-out for SkyRover private edge segments

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's Private offering but need to request a scoped SLA exception for parts of our edge network that we operate and maintain (on-prem edge boxes and regional transit managed by SkyRover). Specifically: 

- We cannot accept a latency SLO that attributes tail latency to Redwood for any hop that leaves our managed WAN (edge -> regional peel) — that segment is under our control and has variable satellite links.
- For KMS-related key retrieval delays originating from our HSM proxies, we ask that those incidents be excluded from Redwood's uptime calculations unless Redwood-managed components can be demonstrated at fault.
- During incident reviews we can provide runbook logs and router/switch telemetry but need a clear definition of what constitutes sufficient evidence and an expedited intake channel for protracted incidents.

Procurement would like an initial position from Redwood by end of week because our SOW and purchasing timeline are tight. I'm attaching a current network diagram and our onboarding runbook excerpt.

Attachments: SkyRover_network_diagram_v2.pdf (network diagram), edge-runbook.md (runbook excerpt)

Can you confirm the information you need and the contractual mechanism (appendix, schedule) you'd prefer for a carve-out?

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure
SkyRover AI

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@skyrover.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for SkyRover private edge segments

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the materials; got both attachments. Short answer: we can accommodate a scoped SLA exclusion for customer-operated edge segments, but we'll need a concrete evidence & audit process and a narrowly worded carve-out that preserves our operational commitments. Proposed next steps: 

1) Internal alignment (we'll scope the carve-out language with Legal and Security).
2) Technical sync — 60m call to walk your runbook, clarify where telemetry will come from, and agree on the list of metrics/artifacts that will be considered authoritative.
3) Draft appendix — Legal will circulate suggested language; we'll aim to keep it as an appendix to the Master Service Agreement to avoid redoing the whole SLA.

Requests for your team before the call: 
- Confirm desired numeric latency thresholds for customer-facing SLAs (e.g., P50/P95 targets you expect Redwood to meet excluding your segment).
- Confirm the exact ASN/site list for the edge boxes and the timeframe for handing over runbook logs during an incident (our standard is 72 hours, but we can discuss).

Kimberly (legal) and Vivek (solutions/CS) are cc'd — Kimberly will take the lead on the contractual wording and Vivek on the technical evidence side. I can run the initial appendix draft through Procurement if you prefer.

I have availability for the technical sync tomorrow between 9:30–11:30 PT or Friday 10–12 PT. What works for you?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@skyrover.ai>
Date: 2027-10-29T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for SkyRover private edge segments

Neha / Vivek —

Looping in my initial legal position. I'm copying Elena for transparency but the language below is our starting point; we'll iterate. Quoting the ask for context: 

> "We cannot accept a latency SLO that attributes tail latency to Redwood for any hop that leaves our managed WAN..."

Suggested contractual approach: an SLA Appendix titled "Customer-Operated Edge Exclusions" that: 

- Defines "Customer-Controlled Edge Segment" by explicit site/ASN list and ingress/egress interfaces (the list must be mutually agreed and appended to the Appendix).
- States that Redwood's latency and availability SLOs exclude incidents where the root cause, as demonstrated by mutually accepted evidence, is isolated to the Customer-Controlled Edge Segment. 
- Requires the Customer to provide telemetry within 72 hours of an incident and grants Redwood the right to request additional logs/evidence for up to 14 days to complete RCA. 
- Provides an escalation path (technical review meeting within 5 business days) and an external adjudication step (third-party network forensics) if parties disagree on attribution — costs are borne by the losing party unless otherwise agreed.

Please note: security must sign off on the telemetry/evidence requirements (hashing, log retention windows, and redaction allowances). I'll prepare a tracked draft (proposed-sla-carveout-clause.docx) that maps to our standard appendix template.

Questions for the technical sync: 
- What exact telemetry formats can SkyRover export (NetFlow, sFlow, packet captures, systemd-journal exports)?
- Will SkyRover permit temporary read-only access to their edge logging endpoints during the post-incident review?

I'll attach the draft clause and run it by Security and Contracts.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-sla-carveout-clause.docx

---

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@skyrover.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@skyrover.ai>
Date: 2027-10-30T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for SkyRover private edge segments

Hi Neha / Kimberly / Vivek —

Thanks — we agree to the approach. A few clarifications up front: 

- Telemetry formats: we can provide NetFlow v9 + per-site packet captures for targeted windows; full packet capture retention is limited to 14 days.
- Read-only access: not directly, but we can provide sanitized exports and a live session with an on-call engineer to walk them through any logs.
- Latency expectations: for our user-facing services we need Redwood to meet P50 < 60ms and P95 < 180ms measured from Redwood ingress to backend, exclusive of our edge-UDP transit (we'll supply the measurement IPs).

Procurement asks that we lock an appendix template in the SOW — we'll sign a mutually agreed appendix and proceed with a pilot. I've attached the onboarding checklist and put the proposed HubSpot deal notes in the DocuSign envelope for the SOW.

Available for the technical call Friday 11:00 PT; please send an invite.

Elena Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure, SkyRover AI

Attachments: SkyRover_onboarding_checklist.xlsx
